If the switch is set to LO (down), the signal measured at input 1 is a static LOW..
If the switch is set to HI (center), the signal measured at input 1 is a static HIGH.
With switch S1 in the pulsed position (up), the same square wave measured at F1 is measured at Input 1.
The three square waves are sent to switches S1, S2 and S3. Each switch is a three position slide switch.
Note, if the potentiometer on the clock circuit is changed, these three output signals will change.
The three outputs are monitored with an oscilloscope at test points F1, F2 and F3.
The square wave is sent to the frequency divider circuit that uses a counter to produce three square waves of different frequency.
Adjusting the potentiometer changes the frequency of the output square wave.
Placing an oscilloscope at the clock's output allows you to monitor the square wave produced.
The clock circuit is designed to produce a square wave output that is varied by the frequency adjust potentiometer.
